title: epan+UI: Add display filter translators
description:
Add a display filter translation API to epan. Add a built-in translator
for pcap filters and a Falco rule translator to the Falco bridge plugin.

Add "Copy / Display filter as <translator>" menu items to Wireshark and
Logray.

notes.body: assigned to @geraldcombs
marked this merge request as **draft**

This started out as a Falco rule translator for Logray, but I generalized the code and added a pcap filter translator. It's still a bit rough, but it's usable enough for testing I wanted to give people a chance to comment.

The pcap filter translator sounds like a good idea in theory, but it would be nice to know how useful people think it will be in practice.

It works well for the filters I tried it with, and was disabled whenever it couldn't apply.

This can be useful - I personally don't use capture filters much as I'm usually looking at small amounts of traffic and don't want to miss anything useful.

I don't know if people use stored capture filters (Captures | Capture filters...) much - it might be nice to add an convenient way to add generated entries there, but I think its easy enough to paste this string in.

Unsurprisingly, "Edit->Copy->Display Filter as pcap filter" doesn't work with field references:

`ip.src == ${ip.src}` translates to `ip src REFERENCE`.

The same sort of issue makes #19138 tricky. The fix for #17599 - dealing with field references when a field appears multiple times in a packet - means that `dfilter_macro_apply` is not the step that loads the field references. But that's because simple text substitution doesn't entirely work - `ip.src == ${ip.src}` needs to be translated to something like `ip.src == A or ip.src == B` or `ip.src in {A, B}` when both A and B are matches.

If that problem is solved for here, it could also be useful for #19138. As it stands some of this could be useful anyway for the `copy the current filter but with macro substitution`.

Translation to BPF probably doesn't work correctly for `vlan` and `mpls`, because they don't commute in BPF - `vlan and ip` and `ip and vlan` are the same display filter expression, but are not the same pcap BPF filter.

More realistically, if `vlan.id` were supported, `vlan 100 && vlan 200` and `vlan 200 && vlan 100` are not the same in BPF but `vlan.id == 100 && vlan.id == 200` are in display filter. The BPF expressions translate to `vlan.id#1 == 100 && vlan.id#2 == 200` and `vlan.id#1 == 200 && vlan.id#2 == 100`.

In similar silly filter tricks,

`ip.src == ip.dst` won't translate into something meaningful as a capture filter, but has occasional value as a display filter.
I added a check for the the RHS of a comparison not being a field value.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -30,6 +30,8 @@ representations for numeric fields).
 
 Display filter functions can be implemented as runtime-loadable C plugins.
 
+Display filters can be translated to pcap filters using menu:Copy[Display filter as pcap filter] if each display filter field has a corresponding pcap filter equivalent.
+
 Custom columns can be defined using any valid field expression, such as
 display filter functions, slices, arithmetic calculations, logical tests,
 raw byte addressing, and the layer modifier.

@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@ set(DFILTER_PUBLIC_HEADERS
 	dfilter-int.h
 	dfilter-loc.h
 	dfilter-plugin.h
+	dfilter-translator.h
 	dfunctions.h
 	drange.h
 	syntax-tree.h
@@ -38,6 +39,7 @@ set(DFILTER_NONGENERATED_FILES
 	dfilter-macro.c
 	dfilter-macro-uat.c
 	dfilter-plugin.c
+	dfilter-translator.c
 	dfunctions.c
 	dfvm.c
 	drange.c

@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+/** @file
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ *
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <glib.h>
+#include <epan/dfilter/syntax-tree.h>
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+/* The run-time logic of the dfilter function */
+typedef bool (*DFTranslator)(stnode_t *root_node, GString *translated);
+
+
+/** Initialize our built-in translators
+ */
+void dfilter_translator_init(void);
+
+/** Clean up our built-in translators
+ */
+void dfilter_translator_cleanup(void);
+
+/** Register a display filter translator
+ * @param translator_name A unique, proper name for the translator, suitable for display.
+ * @param translator A function which will handle translating the syntax tree.
+ * @return true on success, false on failure.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+bool register_dfilter_translator(const char *translator_name, DFTranslator translator);
+
+/** Deregister a display filter translator
+ * @param translator_name The name provided in register_dfilter_translator.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void deregister_dfilter_translator(const char *translator_name);
+
+/** Get the current translator list
+ * @return A NULL terminated array of translator names.
+ * The return value must be g_freed, but the names themselves must not be g_freed.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+char **get_dfilter_translator_list(void);
+
+/** Translate a display filter.
+ *
+ * The root node and data pointer will be passed to the
+ * @param translator_name The name of a registered translator.
+ * @param dfilter The Wireshark display filter to translate.
+ * @return A translated filter or rule on success, NULL on failure.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+const char *translate_dfilter(const char *translator_name, const char *dfilter);
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif /* __cplusplus */

@@ -102,6 +102,15 @@ dfilter_compile_full(const char *text, dfilter_t **dfp,
 				DF_EXPAND_MACROS|DF_OPTIMIZE, \
 				__func__)
 
+struct stnode;
+
+/** Build a syntax tree for a filter
+ * @param text A display filter.
+ * @return The root node of a syntax tree on success or NULL on failure.
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+struct stnode *dfilter_get_syntax_tree(const char *text);
+
 /* Frees all memory used by dfilter, and frees
  * the dfilter itself. */
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC
